title: Stereotypical details used to explain death
article: Once again, a person of aboriginal descent has been characterized in a stereotypical manner in the pages of your publication.
The story detailing how police shot and killed Keldon McMillan (Deadly shootout, SP May 22) contained a telling indication of how Metis people are portrayed in the media.

The bulk of the the story contained accounts of McMillan's friends, who attested to the positive contributions he had made to his community. Obviously, there is more to the portrait of this individual than was revealed in this story.

However, when describing how McMillan's physical stature may have contributed to the police's decision to shoot him, size apparently wasn't the only factor. According to the story, the fact that McMillan was "240 pounds, muscular and bald" wasn't imposing in and of itself to police. Rather, his intimidating state as a Metis person was considered noteworthy.
Relations between aboriginal people and the police in Saskatchewan have long been characterized by mistrust, a state that has led to violence on several occasions of late.
Characterizations such as the one described above perpetuate the belief that Metis or First Nations people are dangerous and must be viewed with suspicion and alarm.
Isn't it time that we acknowledge and celebrate the many positive achievements and contributions that aboriginal citizens make to our communities? That would be a story worth telling.
